title: Air Density Ratio Explorer
description: The learner calculates the density ratio for four temperature and altitude conditions and uses it to correct static pressure between catalog and job conditions (multiply to predict, divide to select), checking each answer against density ratio curves for 0, 2,000, 5,000 and 8,000 ft.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Air density

Air temperature

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Density ratio and the correction of fan static pressure for temperature and altitude
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the density ratio for a stated air temperature and site altitude, and use it to correct a static pressure between catalog and job conditions, to within ±0.005 on the ratio and ±0.03 in. wg on the pressure.
prerequisites: Air density and standard air (70°F, sea level, 0.075 lb/ft³)

accessibility.notes: Chart canvas has role=img and an aria-label; verdicts go to role=status feedback boxes and FP.announce (aria-live); the marker readout is aria-live; ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and progress chips pair with colour; each curve has its own colour, dash pattern and point shape; Enter checks and goes to the next challenge; arrow keys move the sliders.

controls.label: Air temperature
controls.purpose: −20 to 600°F, step 10, default 70; moves the marker

controls.purpose: 0 to 10,000 ft, step 500, default 0; moves the marker

controls.label: Actual static pressure / Catalog SP to select at
controls.purpose: The corrected pressure in in. wg (challenges 1 and 2)

equations: Actual SP = catalog SP x DR
Catalog SP for selection = required actual SP / DR
rules: Ratio correct when |answer - model| <= 0.005; pressure when |answer - model| <= 0.03 in. wg (unrounded model)
Two attempts per entry; an empty or non-numeric entry does not use an attempt
Ratios displayed to 3 decimals, pressures to 2, density to 4
Mastery: 6 of 6 entries correct within two attempts each
assumptions: Dry air; altitude sets the barometric pressure through the standard atmosphere
limitations: Numeric ratio readouts are hidden until challenge 4 is finished, so the chart is a sanity check and not an answer key

sources: Equation and challenge values: Chapter 1 sections 'Air Density', 'Air Temperature' and 'Altitude'
Catalog pressures in challenges 1 and 2: illustrative values, labeled so in the sim

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Estimate from the curve, calculate, check with rule-specific feedback, then explore the shape of the relationship
keyQuestions: Why must temperature be absolute (T + 460) in the density ratio?
When do you multiply by the density ratio and when do you divide?
Does a fan move less CFM in thin air?
commonMisconceptions: Hot air or high altitude reduces the CFM a fan moves at a given speed; in fact CFM is unchanged and pressure and power fall.
The temperature correction can be done in °F directly (70 ÷ 250) instead of absolute degrees.
To select a fan for thin air you multiply the required pressure by the density ratio, when you must divide.
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Entries correct: n of 6'; mastery is 6 of 6 correct within two attempts each.
Explore mode is not evidence of mastery
